gdp_level.description: The total value of everything Saudi Arabia produces in a year, at current prices, on a rolling four-quarter basis. Oil output and prices move it sharply.
gdp_level.dollar: “Dollarise” converts each point at that year's average riyal rate per US dollar (World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF); the riyal has been pegged at 3.75 per dollar since 1986, so the rate barely moves.
gdp_level.real: “Make it real” swaps this to Saudi Arabia's real (constant-price) GDP series. This strips out the effect of price changes, including oil prices, so it shows changes in output volume.
gdp_level.source: OECD quarterly national accounts (GASTAT) · GDP at current prices, riyals, seasonally adjusted, shown as a rolling four-quarter sum.

gdp_real.description: GDP adjusted for inflation, at constant prices, so changes reflect real output rather than price changes.
gdp_real.dollar: “Dollarise” converts each point at that year's average riyal rate per US dollar (World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF); the riyal has been pegged at 3.75 per dollar since 1986, so the rate barely moves.
gdp_real.real: This IS the “Make it real” series, toggling it off shows GDP at current (nominal) prices instead.
gdp_real.source: OECD quarterly national accounts (GASTAT) · GDP at constant prices, riyals, seasonally adjusted, shown as a rolling four-quarter sum.

gdp_growth.description: How much the economy grew or shrank compared with the previous three months, in real terms. Oil output moves it sharply: in the second quarter of 2026 oil activities fell by about a quarter on a year earlier as crude exports were disrupted.
gdp_growth.dollar: A growth rate (%) is currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.
gdp_growth.real: This is already a real (inflation-adjusted) growth rate as published, “Make it real” has no additional effect on it.
gdp_growth.source: OECD quarterly national accounts (GASTAT) · real GDP, change on the previous quarter, seasonally adjusted.

cpi.description: How much consumer prices are rising compared with a year ago, on the General Authority for Statistics' consumer price index.
cpi.source: OECD prices database (GASTAT) · consumer price index, all items, change on the same month a year earlier, computed from the index.

cpi_mom.description: How much consumer prices changed in the month. A monthly change is not the annual rate divided by twelve: it moves with one-off price changes that the annual rate smooths out.
cpi_mom.source: OECD prices database (GASTAT) · consumer price index, all items, change on the previous month, computed from the index.

policy_rate.description: The repo rate, the Saudi Central Bank's main policy rate. With the riyal pegged to the US dollar, SAMA moves it in step with the US Federal Reserve rather than setting it for domestic conditions.
policy_rate.source: BIS central bank policy rates (WS_CBPOL, M.SA, extended with the daily series D.SA) · SAMA repo rate, end of month, from January 2000 (the start of BIS's official repo-rate series); the current month shows the latest rate.

unemployment.description: The share of the labour force who want a job and are actively looking but can't find one, all residents, as the International Labour Organization estimates it each year. GASTAT's own quarterly survey rate for the total population is close to this; the rate for Saudi nationals alone, which Vision 2030 targets refer to, is considerably higher.
unemployment.source: World Bank SL.UEM.TOTL.ZS · unemployment, total, ILO modelled estimate, annual. GASTAT's quarterly survey figures are not yet in a database this site can read.

exports.description: The value of goods Saudi Arabia sells to the rest of the world each month, in riyals; mostly crude oil and oil products.
exports.dollar: “Dollarise” converts each point at that year's average riyal rate per US dollar (World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF); the riyal has been pegged at 3.75 per dollar since 1986, so the rate barely moves.
exports.source: IMF international trade in goods (GASTAT) · exports of goods, FOB, riyals, monthly.

imports.description: The value of goods Saudi Arabia buys from the rest of the world each month, in riyals.
imports.dollar: “Dollarise” converts each point at that year's average riyal rate per US dollar (World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF); the riyal has been pegged at 3.75 per dollar since 1986, so the rate barely moves.
imports.source: IMF international trade in goods (GASTAT) · imports of goods, CIF, riyals, monthly.

trade_balance.description: Exports minus imports of goods each month. The balance moves with oil prices and OPEC+ production decisions. In March 2026 oil exports rose while imports fell by about a quarter on a year earlier, as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz was disrupted.
trade_balance.dollar: “Dollarise” converts each point at that year's average riyal rate per US dollar (World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF); the riyal has been pegged at 3.75 per dollar since 1986, so the rate barely moves.
trade_balance.source: IMF international trade in goods (GASTAT) · exports FOB minus imports CIF, riyals, monthly; ends at the latest month with both.

debt_gdp.description: Everything Saudi Arabia's general government owes, compared with the size of the economy.
debt_gdp.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.
debt_gdp.source: IMF World Economic Outlook GGXWDG_NGDP · general government gross debt, % of GDP, actual years only.

deficit.description: The yearly gap between government spending and revenue, as a share of GDP. Negative means a deficit. Oil revenue drives it.
deficit.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.
deficit.source: IMF World Economic Outlook GGXCNL_NGDP · general government net lending/borrowing, % of GDP, actual years only.

fdi.description: Money invested into Saudi businesses from abroad each year (foreign direct investment), as a share of GDP.
fdi.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.
fdi.source: World Bank BX.KLT.DINV.WD.GD.ZS · % of GDP, annual.

current_account.description: Saudi Arabia's overall balance with the rest of the world, trade in goods and services plus net investment income, as a share of GDP.
current_account.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.
current_account.source: World Bank BN.CAB.XOKA.GD.ZS · % of GDP, annual.

fx_usd.description: How many US dollars SAR 1 buys. The riyal has been pegged at 3.75 per US dollar since 1986, so this barely moves.
fx_usd.source: World Bank series PA.NUS.FCRF · official exchange rate, annual average, shown as US$ per SAR 1 (1 ÷ the published SAR per US$).

gdp_growth_yoy.description: How much the economy grew or shrank compared with the same quarter a year earlier, in real terms, before seasonal adjustment; the figure GASTAT headlines.
gdp_growth_yoy.dollar: A growth rate (%) is currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.
gdp_growth_yoy.real: This is already a real (inflation-adjusted) growth rate as published, “Make it real” has no additional effect on it.
gdp_growth_yoy.source: Computed from OECD quarterly national accounts (GASTAT) · real GDP at constant prices, not seasonally adjusted, change on the same quarter a year earlier.
